speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned waking up frightened; can you describe exactly what you or your child sees or hears during these episodes? Also, does anyone else in the household experience similar events?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmare Disorder. The patient's symptoms of waking up frightened, crying, being consolable, and having clear recall of the event are classic indicators of nightmares, distinguishing them from night terrors where amnesia and inconsolability are typical.
